svg.title: From quantum measurements to a supernova fit
svg.desc: Archived IBM hardware and ideal results land on the same best fit. A separate model study shows shifts in matter density, and a schematic shows how subpopulations are packed onto qubits.

g.text: AEQGA / SUPERNOVA COSMOLOGY
From quantum measurements to a supernova fit
Ωₘ is the fraction of the universe’s energy density in matter. Δχ² is the increase in fit score above the classical minimum.
Where did the hardware fit land?
Pantheon+ likelihood contours · 1 update · 32 candidates per run
Ωₘ
Expansion rate H₀ (km/s/Mpc)
Classical best fit
Hardware and ideal tie
Kingston QPU (1/24 new candidates in view)
Ideal simulation (3/24 in view)
Both retained the best starting candidate. Darker contours indicate better fits.
How did modeled noise shift Ωₘ?
Separate simulator study · 100 updates · 1,024 shots per circuit
Ideal
With Kingston calibration noise
Candidates
Seed
Final matter density fraction Ωₘ
Noise shifted Ωₘ lower in 8 of 12 matched pairs.
This study also fit supernova brightness and used a different data selection.
Parallel qubit packing
Each four-qubit block handles a small group
of candidates. The best candidates are selected
across all groups before the next update.
Illustrated with the Marrakesh simulator layout.
38 connected groups × 4 qubits = 152 of 156 qubits used · 608 candidates per update
Sources Kingston job db5r25imb58s738at2v0 and PR #10 audit · Pantheon+ likelihood archive · IBM noise validation · Marrakesh layout study
The original Kingston compiled circuits are unavailable. Packing was studied in simulation.
